title: RAW UNREVIEWED: corrosive-made gold destroys nature while natural gold restores it in a joined quintessence
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. In Q1 of the retained Sloane73 passage, gold made with corrosives is said to destroy nature, whereas natural gold gathered from mine, earth, or floods is described as incorruptible. The later claim joins natural mineral Sol with the human quinta essencia and assigns preservation/restoration of lost nature and renewal of youth to the joined pair. This proposal preserves a provenance-sensitive effect contrast: corrosive manufacture is destructive; naturally sourced gold contributes to restorative efficacy only in the stated joining. It does not identify any target word or select a target reading.

design.architecture: provenance/process to effect polarity, followed by an explicit joining condition for the restorative branch
constraints: Keep natural-source gold and corrosive-made gold as distinct source descriptions because the passage assigns opposed effects.
Preserve the human quinta essencia as the joined partner in the restorative claim; do not collapse it into the gold alone.
Treat the passage's claims as historical source content, not as scientifically verified efficacy or target meanings.

source_evidence.quote:
Forsoþe quinta essencia superior, þat is to seie, heuene of oure lord god bi him silf / Aloone / ȝeueþ not conseruacioun in þe world, and wondirful influence, but by þe vertue of þe sunne, planetis, and oþere sterris; riȝt so oure quinta essencia, þat is, mannys heuene, wole be maad fair wiþ þe sunne mineralle, fynyd, schynynge, incorruptibile; and euene in qualite þat fier may not appeire, corrumpe, ne distroie. and þis is verry gold of þe myn, of þe erþe, or of þe floodis gaderid /

for gold of alkamy maad with corosyues distroieþ kynde, as aristotle and manye oþere philosophoris prouen /

and þerfore good gold naturel, & of þe myn of þe erbe, is clepid of philosophoris ‘sol’ in latyn; for he is þe sonne of oure heuene, lich as sol þe planet is in þe heuene aboue; for þis planete ȝeueþ to gold his influence, nature, colour, & a substaunce incorruptible.

And oure quinta essencia, mannys heuene, is of þe nature *& þe colour of heuene / And oure sol, þat is, fyn gold of þe myne, schal make it fair, riȝt as sol þe planete makiþ heuene fair / and so þese two togidere ioyned schal ȝeue influence in us, and þe condiciouns of heuene and of heuenly sonne / in as miche as it is possible in deedly nature, conseruacioun and restorynge of nature lost, & renewynge of ȝongþe /
